body: Supervised AI-text detectors report high benchmark accuracy, but it is not clear what their decisions are based on. We analyze a RoBERTa-based detector under semantic, structural, and tokenizer-level perturbations, using the M4 dataset (N = 10,000) and controlled generations (N = 300). When Mistral-7B-Instruct was asked to make machine text sound more human, Verb Diversity rose from 0.77 to 0.92 and the outputs became easier to detect. Detection scores appear to track statistical complexity, which also leads to a 76.3% false-positive rate on formal human writing. As a control, we evaluate event-based Latent Space detection. Paraphrasing changed 87% of its event sequences (Jaccard = 0.067), and homoglyphs altered 70% of the extracted verbs even though extraction still ran (Jaccard = 0.30). Its best domain AUC was 0.577. RoBERTa's robustness seems specific to the features it uses, and structural abstraction did not make detection more robust.
summaryZh: 本文分析了监督式AI文本检测器在面对“人性化”生成文本时的表现。研究发现，当模型被要求模仿人类写作风格时，其统计复杂性增加，反而导致检测器更容易将其识别为机器生成，且在正式人类写作中存在高误报率。该研究揭示了现有检测器依赖统计特征的局限性，并指出结构化抽象等手段难以提升检测鲁棒性。
